div.div: of 5 risk zones are HIGH - immediate action needed before execution begins
With at stake and high-risk zones unresolved, this programme carries the profile of projects that fail after steel is cut. The window to act is now.
1 of 5 risk zones is HIGH - close this gap before tooling begins
With at stake, one unresolved HIGH zone is enough to derail your programme at trial stage. This is recoverable - but only before steel is cut.
No HIGH risk zones - your programme is well positioned
Your governance position is stronger than most programmes at this stage. Protect it - do not let execution pressure override the structured governance that got you here.

div.t: Your design process has not had an independent review. The risk of discovering tooling-incompatible decisions during trials is significant. Once steel is cut, corrections cost more time and money - and some cannot be undone.
Your design process is partially governed. An independent review before tooling begins would reduce downstream exposure and prevent avoidable trial failures.
Your design process is well-governed. Independent checks are planned before tooling begins. This significantly reduces the risk of costly design-related trial failures.

div.div: If not closed before steel is cut
A single failed trial on a medical device programme can delay launch by 6 to 12 months - with no recovery option on a fixed regulatory timeline.
Partial governance means some design decisions will not have been independently validated. These gaps surface at trial stage - when correction costs are already elevated.

div.t: Your programme cost exposure is not fully understood. Trial iterations, rework, and redesign costs have not been budgeted. These costs typically surface when financial commitments are already made and cannot be reversed.
Your cost picture is approximate. Hidden costs may surface at trial stage. A structured cost review before tooling would reduce financial surprises mid-programme.
Your cost framework is defined. Trial and rework budgets are allocated. This significantly reduces financial exposure at trial stage.

div.div: On programmes with multiple moulds, even one additional trial cycle per mould adds significant hidden cost - before any rework is counted.
Approximate cost assumptions are typically based on optimistic scenarios. Real programmes encounter rework, design changes, and additional trials that were not in the original budget.

div.t: Your supplier governance has significant gaps. Toolmaker selection, quality accountability, and programme ownership are not clearly defined. This pattern is present in most programmes that fail at trial stage. It is recoverable - but only before tooling begins.
Your supplier governance is partially in place. Some accountability gaps remain that could create delays at trial stage. Formalising responsibilities before tooling begins will reduce exposure.
Your supplier governance is well-structured. Accountability is defined and toolmaker selection is rigorous. This reduces the risk of trial disputes and delays.

div.div: When quality ownership is not documented, every trial dispute becomes a negotiation. Both sides have already spent money. Neither side wants to absorb the cost. Programmes stall here.
Risk if gaps are not formalised
Partial governance means accountability is assumed rather than documented. At trial stage, assumptions become disputes. Formalise before tooling begins.

div.t: Your quality standard has not been defined before tooling begins. Without a clear quality target, trial buyoff criteria will be disputed and rework cycles will multiply. This is one of the most common causes of extended trial loops.
Your quality standard is partially defined. Formalising the specification before tooling begins will reduce trial disputes and accelerate buyoff.
Your quality standard is clearly defined. This reduces trial buyoff disputes and accelerates programme closure.

div.div: The consequence that cannot be undone
Quality standard not defined before tooling leads to disputed buyoff, repeated trials, and potential programme abandonment after steel is cut.
Partially defined quality standards leave room for interpretation at buyoff. When both parties interpret differently, the result is additional trials and schedule delay.

div.t: Your programme has a fixed deadline with revenue directly at risk. Combined with unresolved governance gaps in other zones, this is the highest-risk combination. A single unplanned trial rework cycle could cost you your market window.
Your delivery timeline has some flexibility but business consequences of delay exist. Resolving governance gaps before tooling begins will protect your launch window.
Your delivery risk is manageable. Your timeline has flexibility and the business impact of delay is limited.

div.div: What a delay actually costs in your situation
A delay on a programme with a hard deadline is not a setback. It is a business-threatening event. Revenue lost in Year 1 cannot be recovered in Year 2.
Why flexibility does not mean safety
Flexible timelines can absorb one delay. They cannot absorb compounding delays from multiple unresolved governance gaps. Address the gaps before tooling begins.
